title: The Thief and His Monkey (தமிழ்)

full_text:
In the bustling port of Alexandria lived a cunning pickpocket who owned a trained monkey of remarkable agility. The monkey had been taught to slip through open high windows, climb up silk curtains, and snatch gold coins, rings, and brooches from dressing tables while the owners were downstairs at dinner. Through this deceitful practice, the thief amassed a fortune in gold without performing a single day of honest labor.

Desiring to enjoy his wealth in safety, the thief boarded a merchant vessel sailing for Constantinople. In his heavy leather belt were sewn a thousand stolen gold dinars, and the monkey sat beside him upon the deck.

As the ship sailed across the sunny waters of the Mediterranean, the thief took out his gold coins to count his treasure, gloating over his cleverness. The monkey, watching his master closely, remembered how he had been trained to snatch glittering objects.

When the thief fell asleep beneath the awning, the monkey seized the heavy purse of a thousand dinars, leaped up the ropes of the mainmast, and perched upon the highest yardarm!

The thief awakened, saw his monkey with the treasure, and turned pale with terror. He whistled, waved nuts and sweetmeats, and pleaded: 'Come down, dear friend! That is our livelihood!'

The monkey chattered merrily, opened the purse, and took out two gold coins. He threw one coin down onto the wooden deck into his master’s lap, and hurled the second coin far out into the azure sea! Again he reached into the purse: one coin dropped to the ship, and the next splashed into the waves.

The passengers and sailors gathered on deck, laughing and cheering as the monkey systematically divided the fortune: one coin for the thief on earth, and one coin returned to the deep waters of the ocean!

When the last coin was thrown, the monkey tossed the empty leather purse into the sea and climbed down to his master. The thief sat among five hundred coins, weeping over his lost half. An aged captain placed a hand upon his shoulder and said: 'Do not weep, brother. The monkey was a wiser judge than the magistrate: five hundred coins were earned by your labor in feeding him, and five hundred were stolen from the innocent. The sea has reclaimed what belonged to greed.'
moral: Ill-gotten gains cannot be concealed forever; justice finds its way through the most unexpected instruments. [TA]
